# E038 -- Peloton Commercial Marketing Guidelines

## Metadata
- **Company:** Peloton (Peloton Interactive, Inc.)
- **Industry:** Fitness / Technology
- **Year:** 2020
- **Source file:** peloton-commercial-marketing-guidelines-2020-pdf.pdf
- **Pages:** 20
- **Language:** EN
- **Pages sampled:** 1-2, 6-7, 12-13

## Brand Strategy
- Titled "Commercial Marketing Guidelines" -- designed for commercial partners, not internal brand teams
- Document focused on how third parties (hotels, gyms, commercial partners) should represent Peloton
- Pre-approval required in writing or electronically for any co-branded promotional use
- Copyright 2019-2020, Peloton Interactive, Inc., 125 W 25th St, 11th Fl, New York, NY 10001

## Logo
- Logo lockup = Peloton logomark + Peloton wordmark (primary logo for most cases)
- Size ratios and spacing between mark and wordmark must never change
- Clearspace: height of wordmark ("Y") on all four sides
- Minimum size: 25px (screen) / 3/8" (print) for lockup; 18px / 1/4" for wordmark; 9px / 1/8" for logomark
- Logo colors: "Peloton Black" or white only, preferably on neutral backgrounds
- Over imagery/video: lockup OK with sufficient contrast; wordmark should NOT be used over imagery/video
- Logomark alone can receive "Peloton Super Red" color treatment -- only logo element that can use red
- Construction grid provided with X/Y proportional system
- Co-branding must be pre-approved

## Typography
- Not covered in sampled pages -- document is partner-focused, likely relies on brand voice section instead

## Color
- "Peloton Black" -- primary logo and brand color
- "Peloton Super Red" -- accent color, restricted to logomark only
- White -- secondary logo option
- Neutral backgrounds preferred
- Brand Colors section referenced in TOC (p.10)

## Graphics
- Not covered beyond logo system in sampled pages

## Photography
- Extremely detailed product photography specifications for Peloton Bike:
  - Seat and handlebars must be level with each other
  - Specific knob orientations: Knobs A and B facing south, Knob C facing north
  - Pedal bar aligned with cross bar logo
  - Default Bike setup: F (under touch screen), 28 (seat height), E (seat depth)
  - Resistance knob logo must be visible depending on angle
  - Minimum 5 feet distance between Bike and environment
  - Shoot from right side only
  - Do NOT shoot at max handlebar height, hard profile, on mat, or with non-Peloton equipment
- Product Photography section is unusually prescriptive

## Tone of Voice
- Brand Voice section (p.04) and "How We Speak" referenced in TOC
- Social media copy examples: "Experience immersive cardio that keeps you coming back for more" / "When you stay with us, you can stay on track towards your fitness goals" / "Join live or on-demand studio classes"
- Voice is aspirational, active, and fitness-focused
- Do not insert non-approved brand hashtags
- Pre-written copy variants provided for partners to use

## Outliers
- This is a commercial/partner marketing guide, not a comprehensive brand identity document -- designed for hotels, gyms, and B2B partners
- Extraordinarily specific product photography requirements (knob directions, exact bike settings, shooting angle restrictions)
- Pre-written social media copy provided for partners -- unusual level of control over third-party messaging
- Pre-approval required for any co-branded use -- reflects tight brand control
- Only 20 pages but covers logo, photography, social, environmental, and digital -- efficiently scoped for its purpose

## Quality Score
- **Score: 3/5** -- A tightly scoped commercial partner guide that excels at practical implementation: logo usage, product photography specs, social media templates, and environmental design. The product photography section is exceptionally detailed. However, this is not a full brand identity system -- it is a partner toolkit. Lacks typography, comprehensive color system, brand strategy depth, and is designed for external compliance rather than creative inspiration.
